acceptance.given: A caller invokes either the public CLI or Python entry for one input and policy.

oracle.expected: The invoked entry returns structured result data representing the invocation outcome.
forbidden: The invocation returns an unstructured result or no structured result.
oracle.observable: Structured result object emitted by the public CLI or Python entry for the invocation.

acceptance.then: The public entry returns a structured result.
acceptance.when: The invocation completes and its result is inspected.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the public CLI and Python entry structured-result selector for a representative invocation; observe failure when either entry emits no structured result or an unstructured payload.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Both public entry points emit structured result data for each invocation outcome.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing public invocation arguments and structured result compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: Entry invocation transitions to a structured result object.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Both public entry invocations return parseable structured result data.

acceptance.given: An invocation has produced zero or more diagnostics.

oracle.expected: The structured result contains a bounded diagnostics list and every diagnostic record exposes rule, path, and message values.
forbidden: A diagnostic record omits the rule, path, or message field.
oracle.observable: Parsed diagnostics collection and each record's rule, path, and message fields during result validation.

acceptance.then: The result contains only a bounded, field-complete diagnostics list.
acceptance.when: The returned structured result is validated for diagnostics shape and bounds.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the diagnostics result-shape selector for an invocation producing diagnostics; fail when the list exceeds its bound or any item lacks rule, path, or message.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Diagnostics are returned as a bounded list with rule, path, and message fields on every record.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Retain existing diagnostic consumers while enforcing bounded, field-complete records.

slice_hint.state_transition: Diagnostic generation transitions to a bounded, schema-complete collection.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every returned diagnostics list is within the configured bound and each item has rule, path, and message values.

acceptance.given: The same input bytes and policy are available for two public-entry runs.

oracle.expected: Both runs yield equivalent structured output in the contract's sorted form, with no run-varying fields.
forbidden: Equivalent inputs and policy produce differing results.
The repeated output is not sorted as required by the contract.
oracle.observable: Canonicalized comparison of two serialized public-entry results, including ordering and absence of timestamps or environment secrets.

acceptance.then: Repeated identical runs yield equivalent sorted output.
acceptance.when: The two results are canonicalized, sorted, and compared byte-for-byte.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the repeated-invocation determinism selector twice with identical input bytes and policy; fail when canonical sorted outputs differ or contain run-varying fields.

affected_subjects: Public CLI and Python entry output determinism
slice_hint.behavior_change: Canonicalize and sort public-entry structured output so identical input bytes and policy produce equivalent results across runs.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve public entry arguments and result fields while stabilizing ordering and run invariance.

slice_hint.state_transition: Identical invocations transition to equivalent canonical sorted result representations.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Canonical serialized outputs from two identical runs compare equal and contain no timestamps or environment secrets.

acceptance.given: The public entry receives malformed JSON, an unreadable target, an out-of-root target, duplicate keys, or an unsupported contract version.

oracle.expected: Each named invalid-input case returns a structured non-passing result and uses the corresponding failure semantics.
forbidden: An unsupported contract version returns pass.
oracle.observable: Per-case structured result status and failure semantics observed while validating all five invalid-input cases.

acceptance.then: Each named invalid-input case is represented as a non-passing result.
acceptance.when: The public entry processes each malformed, unreadable, out-of-root, duplicate-key, or unsupported-version case and its status is evaluated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the five invalid-input selectors and fail if any malformed JSON, unreadable target, out-of-root target, duplicate-key, or unsupported-version case returns pass.

affected_subjects: Public CLI and Python entry validation boundary
slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject each named malformed or unauthorized input with a structured non-passing result and failure semantics.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Maintain public invocation compatibility while preserving non-passing semantics for all named invalid-input classes.

slice_hint.state_transition: Invalid input transitions from entry processing to a structured non-passing result with failure semantics.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: All five named invalid-input cases are rejected as non-passing by the public entry validation path.
